item.title: Kane prematurely announced as Ballon d'Or winner - but he wasn't only one
item.description: Harry Kane has become the first Englishman since 2001 to win the Ballon d'Or [Getty Images] Harry Kane was crowned winner of the men's Ballon d'Or on Monday night, but a few hours earlier that confirmation appeared to have been announced prematurely. At 17:15 GMT, an article from the award's official website titled 'Harry Kane wins the 2026 Ballon d'Or' began to circulate online. The widespread sharing of the article caused confusion online, with some wondering whether France Football - the organisers of the award - had fallen short at the final hurdle of keeping the winner, who was voted for by journalists at the end of September, under wraps. That was until further digging on the Ballon d'Or website revealed that some of the other favourites to win the award - including Barcelona's Lamine Yamal, Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe - also had similar pieces penned and published about them. When asked about the articles by BBC Sport, a Ballon d'Or spokesperson said: "Some profiles of nominees prepared by BallonDor.com were inadvertently published online. "These articles had been prepared for all nominees and should in no way be considered as an indication of the final results or rankings." By 17:40, the articles about Kane and Mbappe had been removed from the website. Similar articles were also written about London City Lionesses star Alexia Putellas and Barcelona's Ewa Pajor. Putellas went on to be officially confirmed as the winner of the women's Ballon d'Or. That premature announcement may have sparked some excitement in Kane that this could be his year, but he only had to wait a little longer to find out for sure. item.title: Putellas wins record-equalling third Ballon d'Or
item.description: Alexia Putellas won four trophies with Barcelona last season and 38 over the course of 14 years [Getty Images] Spain midfielder Alexia Putellas has won the Ballon d'Or Feminin for a record-equalling third time, keeping the prize in Spanish hands for a sixth consecutive year. Putellas, 32, captained Barcelona to Champions League glory as part of a quadruple in 2025-26, before joining Women's Super League (WSL) side London City Lionesses in July . She joins Spain team-mate Aitana Bonmati on three Ballon d'Or Feminin crowns - her former Barcelona colleague won the award in 2023, 2024 and 2025 after Putellas did so in 2021 and 2022. The past six Ballons d'Or have been won by the Spanish pair, with Norway's Ada Hegerberg (2018) and Megan Rapinoe of the United States (2019) the only non-Spaniards to claim the prize. Putellas' latest victory caps a remarkable return to the pinnacle of world football after suffering a career-threatening anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury in 2022. "All the boys and girls around the world - if you love football and if you want to play football, play football. It doesn't matter if you're a boy or if you're a girl," Putellas said. "Doesn't matter where you come from. Don't listen if someone tells you, you can't do it. Believe in yourself." She collected the most votes from an international panel of journalists across Fifa's top-50 ranked countries, with Barcelona striker Ewa Pajor coming second and Manchester City forward Khadija Shaw third. Meanwhile, England captain Harry Kane won the men's Ballon d'Or , becoming the first English player to do so since Michael Owen in 2001. The numbers don't lie While Barcelona are always overwhelming favourites to win the three competitions on offer in Spain, Putellas' performances last season showed that she is still among the world's elite. Nicknamed 'La Reina' - meaning the queen - Putellas scored 21 goals and provided 13 assists in all competitions, ranking her third and second respectively among players across Europe's top five leagues. Seven of those goals came in the Women's Champions League as Barcelona claimed a fourth continental title in six seasons. Only Pernille Harder (eight), Alessia Russo (nine) and Ewa Pajor (11) scored more, all of whom are strikers by trade. But Putellas' contributions to Barcelona's attacking play went far beyond scoring goals herself. In Liga F - which Barcelona won for a seventh consecutive season - she finished joint-sixth for assists (seven) and fourth for open-play chances created (40). Across Europe's top five leagues, only Claudia Pina (199), Vicky Lopez (183) and Georgia Stanway (168) recorded more sequence involvements ending in an open-play shot than Putellas (151). In all competitions, she created more chances (89, 19 of which were big chances) and completed more passes ending in the final third (965) than any other player in Liga F, the Champions League, Copa de la Reina and Supercopa de Espana. item.title: Kane ends England's 25-year Ballon d'Or wait - how he bucked the trend
item.description: Harry Kane broke Bayern Munich's goalscoring record for a season in his third campaign at the club [Getty Images] Harry Kane has become the first English player to win the Ballon d'Or since Michael Owen in 2001 after being crowned the world's best player at a ceremony in London. The 33-year-old Bayern Munich striker is the fifth Englishman to win in total, with Stanley Matthews (1956), Bobby Charlton (1966) and Kevin Keegan (1978 and 1979) the others. Denis Law of Scotland (1964) and Northern Ireland's George Best (1968) are the other winners from the United Kingdom. Real Madrid and France forward Kylian Mbappe finished second, while Barcelona and Spain attacker Lamine Yamal completed the top three. "Not many people would have thought it, and maybe even I wouldn't have thought I'd be this far," Kane told Dazn. "I had to go through many ups and downs, especially early in my career. I was never the person that people thought was going to be the superstar like some of the guys now. "I had to bide my time and work hard, a lot of times it was me against my own mind and I had to come through it, I had to show self-belief, determination. "I think that grounded me even when I did make it at the highest level to keep improving and keep getting better." England manager Thomas Tuchel said he was "delighted" to see Kane win the award as he hailed the forward's success as a "huge honour". Prince William, meanwhile, said the former Tottenham Hotspur player was a "brilliant captain" and "remarkable player". Kane scored 61 goals in 51 club matches last season, the most a Bayern player has ever struck in one campaign. Including England matches, it was 73 goals - plus eight assists - in 65 matches. Only one player at a club in Europe's top five leagues has ever scored more goals in a season. But he wins it despite not lifting either of football's biggest prizes last season, having lost in both the World Cup and Champions League semi-finals. Remarkably the Three Lions captain becomes the first Bayern player to win the Ballon d'Or since Karl-Heinz Rummenigge in 1981. To celebrate Kane's success, the Wembley arches were lit up in gold on Monday night. BBC Sport looks at why Kane won it and how unusual it is to do so without securing one of those major trophies. England's greatest international? Kane is now a serious contender Putellas wins record-equalling third Ballon d'Or Kane's record-breaking 2025-26 season In terms of trophies, Kane may have 'only' lifted the German double last season. But that more than doubled his career trophy total - having also won the Bundesliga the season before. But in terms of individual output Kane - whose previous best Ballon d'Or finish was 10th - was unmatched last season. His 61 goals in all competitions for Bayern was 19 more than any other player in Europe's top five leagues managed. item.title: Myles Garrett’s latest injury update doesn’t help Rams
item.description: Myles Garrett has not played for the Los Angeles Rams since Week 1 and the team still is not sure if the edge rusher will return to the field any time soon. Sean McVay was asked about Garrett returning for the Los Angeles Chargers game on Sunday, and the head coach said that he wasn’t sure if L.A.‘s superstar offseason acquisition would practice this week or not. McVay said needs to meet with Reggie Scott, the Rams’ Senior Vice President of Sports Medicine and Performance, before he makes any type of determination. The Rams have not made a determination yet on whether or not to open the practice windows for Myles Garrett or Terrance Ferguson, per Sean McVay. — Nate Atkins (@NateAtkins_) October 26, 2026 McVay was asked about both Garrett and tight end Terrance Ferguson potentially making a return to practice this week, but answered that he wasn’t prepared to answer yet. “I’m not sure yet. I’m not decided on those things.” A follow-up question was asked with regard to when McVay would know whether or not either player would practice this week. McVay only offers further that he’ll meet with the medical team and go from there. McVay doesn’t offer any insight to how he thinks that meeting will go, just that he needs to meet with them before making a decision. “Once I get with Reggie and talk about the approach for the week. Then we’ll just kinda follow their guidance based on where he’s at and how he’s feeling.” It could be gamesmanship, it could be McVay wanted to have genuine deniability for this presser about whether Garrett will play this week or not, but at some point the team will need to make a decision on Garrett. And hopefully soon because the team invested a lot into him as an addition for a defense that is lacking serious firepower upfront this season. The Rams traded a first-round pick, Jared Verse, and more to to get Garrett . He hasn’t played in a game since Week 1, as the 2025 sack leader has yet to notch one single sack or tackle for his new team. The longer Garrett doesn’t suit up, the harder it will be for the Rams to stay afloat in a tough 2026 season where the Rams need to go on a run to make Garrett’s return worth it from a playoff perspective. By the time Garrett is ready, if he’s ready, will there be a point to playing this season? Or, will it better to wait for 2027? As McVay might say, “I’m not sure yet. I’m not decided on those things.”

item.title: 49ers' Christian McCaffrey has mild hamstring strain. Will he return after bye week?
item.description: San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey runs against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday. (Danny Karnik/Associated Press) San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan said running back Christian McCaffrey suffered a mild hamstring strain during Sunday's 29-20 loss to the Atlanta Falcons. Shanahan is "pretty optimistic" McCaffrey will be available for the 49ers' Nov. 8 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders, the team's next game following a Week 8 bye. "We think so, with it just being (a mild strain)," Shanahan said Monday afternoon. "Never know for sure, but we're pretty optimistic about it. So is he." Not long after totaling 69 yards and a touchdown Sunday on the 49ers' opening drive, McCaffrey was seen stretching on the sideline and pressing a massage gun to his left hamstring area. He then entered the blue tent for an extended period in the second quarter before jogging to the locker room. He reentered to start the second half but was significantly hampered, ending the afternoon with just 34 snaps, his second-lowest number of the season. After his explosive opening drive, McCaffrey recorded just 10 rushing yards and 21 receiving yards. Postgame, McCaffrey told reporters that his leg "just died" on him. "I was trying to get it going for the whole rest of the game, but it just sucks trying to play like that. But I know I'll be all right." No kicker change: Shanahan said the 49ers are not planning to try out any kickers during the bye week amid Eddy Piñeiro's continued struggles to convert extra points. "I haven't been told that we are," Shanahan said. "As far as I've heard, we don't have any plans on that right now." Piñeiro is 21 of 25 on extra points this season. He has missed one of his three attempts in each of the last two games. On Sunday, Piñeiro shanked an extra point in the fourth quarter that prevented the 49ers from cutting their deficit to five points. Because of that, when Atlanta converted a field goal to go up nine points in the final minute, the 49ers did not have an opportunity to string together a potential game-tying drive. After the 49ers' 23-20 win over the Washington Commanders on Oct. 19, Shanahan said Piñeiro has "got to make" his extra points. When asked after that game if there was a level of concern with the trend, Shanahan said, "I think everyone knows the answer to that." Asked about his extra-point struggles on Sunday, Piñeiro said he will take the bye week to watch the tape, reassess and start over. Piñeiro is 6-for-9 on field-goal attempts this season. item.title: The hockey world mourns the sudden death of star goaltender at just 31 years old
item.description: The hockey world mourns the sudden death of star goaltender at just 31 years old There are days in the hockey world where the game itself just doesn't matter. Saturday was one of those days. The ECHL, Ohio State University, and the broader hockey community are grieving after learning that former goaltender Sean Romeo passed away at just 31 years old. Romeo died from complications stemming from a stroke he initially suffered on October 15, leaving behind a legacy that stretched far beyond the crease. For those unfamiliar with Romeo's story, this was a guy who did everything the right way. He wasn't just a talented netminder. He was the kind of person who made everyone around him better, and even in death, he continued to give. Romeo was an organ donor, and his heart, lungs, liver, and kidneys were donated to give others a second chance at life. That tells you everything you need to know about the type of human being he was. A Career Built on Excellence Romeo's hockey journey took him from the University of Maine to Ohio State, where he truly made his mark. After transferring and sitting out the 2016-17 season due to NCAA transfer rules at the time, he wasted no time establishing himself as one of the best goaltenders in Buckeyes history. In 2017-18, he earned Second Team All-Big Ten honors and became the first Ohio State player ever named a Mike Richter Award semifinalist. He was also selected as the Most Outstanding Player of the NCAA Midwest Regional that year, backstopping the Buckeyes to their first NCAA semifinal appearance since 1998. The records he set at Ohio State speak for themselves. Romeo posted a school-record shutout streak of 204 minutes and 27 seconds in November 2018 and became the first goalie in program history to record shutouts in three consecutive starts. He finished his career fourth all-time in goals-against average (2.22), tied for fourth in save percentage (.919), and tied for fifth with five career shutouts. His 22-win campaign in 2018 ranks tied for second in a single season in Ohio State history, with his 2.06 GAA and .927 save percentage that year both placing fourth all-time. But Romeo wasn't just a star on the ice. He was a standout in the classroom as well, earning the NCAA Elite 90 Award for having the highest grade-point average among all student-athletes at the 2018 Frozen Four. He was a three-time Ohio State Scholar-Athlete, a two-time Academic All-Big Ten honoree, and a Senior CLASS Award Top 15 candidate in 2019. He earned his bachelor's degree in finance from Ohio State in the spring of 2019 and was part of both the 2018 Frozen Four squad and the 2019 Big Ten Championship team. Life After College Hockey After wrapping up his collegiate career, Romeo pursued his dream of playing professionally. He suited up for seven different ECHL clubs over a 30-game professional career, including stints with Cincinnati, Florida, Adirondack, Norfolk, Indy, South Carolina, and Kansas City. Outside hitter Grace Egan – after missing the previous 13 matches with a serious back injury – subbed in to serve the last point of the set. UW fans greeted the moment with a rousing ovation during a set when the Badgers otherwise did not give much to cheer about. “She was pretty moved by that and pretty emotional afterwards,” Wisconsin coach Kelly Sheffield said. “There was a lot of hard work to get back into that, to be able to get out with her teammates in a match.” That moment and another crowd-pleasing entrance to play briefly in the back row against Michigan have prompted the question of how quickly Egan can return in a more extensive capacity. “The ability of putting together a two-hour match – I’m not sure we’re quite there, but we’re not that far away from there,” Sheffield said at his Oct. 26 press conference. Egan hinted at her return on Oct. 22 with a video shared on Instagram with “I’M BACK” overlaying past footage of her running to the court. Sheffield needs to see more from Egan in the practice gym before she is fully back, though. “She hasn’t been practicing a lot right now,” Sheffield said. “So I think in fairness to her and our team and everything, you got to kind of stack some days in practices to be able to play with freedom and to trust your body and be able to turn it loose. And we’re just in that process.” That being said, Sheffield has already seen Egan “trusting her body more every day.” “It wasn’t too many days ago that there was fear, uncertainty – can I trust this?” Sheffield said.“There are certain body parts that when they fail you without notice, it can stay with you a little bit.” To even be at this point is an accomplishment for Egan considering the severity of the back injury and subsequent recovery. (It was severe enough that she was not on the charter flight with the team to Texas for UW’s Sept. 11-13 nonconference matches.) “She couldn’t be in the practice gym because she couldn’t stand or sit,” Sheffield said. “She wasn’t traveling with us because she couldn’t sit on a plane in that posture. item.title: France Football chief reveals how close the Ballon d'Or race was between Kane and Mbappé
item.description: France Football chief reveals how close the Ballon d'Or race was between Kane and Mbappé Bayern Munich star Harry Kane was named the 2026 Ballon d’Or winner on Monday night, finishing ahead of Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappé. Speaking to L’Équipe afterwards, France Football editor-in-chief Vincent Garcia, who oversees the organisation of the Ballon d’Or, revealed just how close the race between the two had been. “This year, there were several serious contenders. The two closest were the top two, Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappé, and the race between them was decided by very little," Garcia told L'Equipe (via iMiaSanMia). "The points gap between Kane and Mbappé was smaller than the gap between Rodri and Vinícius Júnior in 2024, which was 41 points - and that was already a very narrow margin at the time. It was incredibly close between Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappé in the battle for first place this year. “I was watching the results in real time during the month of the vote. Kylian led the race for a long time, but Harry Kane came back into contention, and in the end, it was decided by a very, very small number of points," he revealed.

item.title: Harry Kane And The Dawn Of A New Soccer Order
item.description: LONDON, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 26: Harry Kane of FC Bayern Munich and England accepts the Men's Ballon d'Or award during the 70th Ballon D'Or Ceremony at Palladium Theatre on October 26, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Jeff Spicer - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images) UEFA via Getty Images For nearly two decades, the Ballon d’Or was defined by a rivalry that transcended soccer. Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo did not simply dominate the game’s most prestigious individual award. They reshaped expectations of greatness, turning extraordinary seasons into the standard against which every other player was measured. Messi and Ronaldo top the all-time rankings with eight and five Ballons d’Or, respectively. Now, with the 33-year-old Harry Kane claiming the prize on Monday night (ahead of Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal) after a remarkable campaign for Bayern Munich and England, the game has another chance to ask a question that has been waiting in the background for years: What comes after Messi and Ronaldo? Kane’s triumph at the London ceremony represents more than a personal milestone or the end of a 25-year wait for an English Ballon d’Or winner. It signals a changing soccer landscape, one in which the sport’s biggest individual prize can once again become a contest between different generations, playing styles and definitions of excellence. “Being in London, it is extra special, it felt like a good omen,” Kane said during his speech. “Thank you to everyone who voted for me, I can imagine it was tough, so thank you.” Kane’s achievement carries a particular significance for English soccer. The last Englishman to win the Ballon d’Or was Michael Owen in 2001, when his pace and goalscoring exploits made him one of the most exciting young strikers in the world at the time. A quarter of a century later, Kane has restored England’s presence at the summit of individual recognition. “It’s just the journey," Kane said. “For any young boy or girl who wants to achieve their dream, anything is possible.” But the significance of this victory extends beyond nationality. Kane’s journey has never followed the conventional path of a superstar. He was not universally regarded as a generational talent in his teen years, nor did he arrive at the top of the game with the mythology that surrounded Messi and Ronaldo. Instead, he built his reputation through persistence, consistency and an almost relentless commitment to improving his skills. Kane’s 73 goals for club and country last season, combined with domestic silverware with Bayern and a prolific World Cup campaign, provide the statistical foundation for his recognition. But the story behind those numbers is equally important: Kane has reached the highest level through evolution rather than instant superstardom. The Messi-Ronaldo era was not merely about individual brilliance. It was about longevity at a level rarely seen in sports. item.description: Spain's Luis de La Fuente won the men's coach of the year (FRANCK FIFE) Harry Kane became England's first Ballon d'Or winner in 25 years in his native city of London on Monday, beating Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe. Alexia Putellas claimed the women's prize for a third time to extend Spain's domination of the award, thanks to her role in leading Barcelona to last season's Champions League before moving to London City Lionesses. The first ever Ballon d'Or ceremony on English soil got off to an inauspicious start as the London traffic caused a delay of nearly an hour, with many of the star names arriving late. But there was a happy ending for the hometown hero as Kane collected the crowning glory of his career to date, becoming the first Englishman to win the award since Michael Owen in 2001. The 33-year-old Bayern Munich forward struck a remarkable 73 goals in 65 games for club and country last season, propelling the German giants to a league and cup double. He also scored six times as England finished third at the World Cup. "I love to represent my country and to bring this trophy back to them and have an English winner I think is something that's really, really special, especially here in London," Kane told AFP. "What a crazy night and I'm really, really happy." Despite being England and Tottenham's all-time record goalscorer, Kane's medal collection is limited to German domestic triumphs. He was on the losing side for Spurs in the 2019 Champions League final against Liverpool and twice tasted bitter defeat in the final of the European Championship with England. But joining Bayern in 2023 and his remarkable goalscoring consistency have earned him the highest individual award in football. "Making the move to Bayern Munich was a big step in my career," Kane told AFP earlier. "Some people saw it as a risk but for me it was always about improving and seeing if I could get better around the team-mates, the team, the club and it has pushed me onto another level. "Being a number nine for Bayern and England you are expected to score goals and to do that the number of times I did last year is something I'm really proud of," he added. - Putellas back on top - The winner in 2021 and 2022, Putellas's third Ballon d'Or caps her return to the top of the women's game after an anterior cruciate ligament injury derailed her rise four years ago. Putellas succeeds Spain team-mate Aitana Bonmati, the winner the past three years whose season was quashed by a leg break. "This is a consequence of all that we achieved last season," said Putellas. "I am really grateful for having been (at Barcelona) 14 seasons as a player, it is something incredible. It was like a perfect story." item.title: Nick Wright: Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker has declined since ‘splitting his time between football and activism’
item.description: Credit: First Things First on FS1 At the height of the Kansas City Chiefs dynasty, kicker Harrison Butker became a symbol for conservative values after discussing his religiously motivated views on family life during a speech at Benedictine College. The 2024 speech became a lightning rod across the media, with everyone from ESPN’s Laura Rutledge to Serena Williams to Eddie Vedder ripping Butker for comments in which he cited “ diabolical lies ” told to women and called “homemaker” “one of the most important titles of all.” The Chiefs stood by Butker: Head coach Andy Reid defended him in the media, and tight end Travis Kelce sidestepped the controversy on his popular podcast. And while Butker continued as the team’s kicker, he also launched a conservative political action committee (PAC) and a menswear brand called Shepherd’s. After a couple decent seasons following the controversial speech, the 31-year-old kicker has made less than 70 percent of his field goals this year and went just 1-for-3 in Kansas City’s Week 7 loss on Sunday Night Football . Reacting to the Chiefs’ loss Monday on First Things First , host Nick Wright, a noted fan of the team, called out Butker’s “activism” as a reason for his decline. “He started splitting his time between football and activism, and he hasn’t been quite as good,” he said. “That is just the timeline of it.” Nick Wright on Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker after 1-3 performance on Sunday Night Football: “He started splitting his time between football and activism, and he hasn’t been quite as good. That is just the timeline of it.” https://t.co/uw97bigoaw — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) October 26, 2026 While Wright also noted Butker’s age, he said he no longer feels as confident when the kicker steps up for a field goal as he did for the entirety of Kansas City’s dynasty. The comments matter not only because they pin Butker’s struggles through the first two months of the season on his off-field work, but also because they sharply diverge from what Wright’s co-host, Chris Broussard, said after Butker’s campus speech in 2024. “Today is so polarizing that people on national television or radio, people are blatantly misinterpreting what people are saying when what they actually said is right there and contradicting what you say,” Broussard said at the time . “With Harrison Butker, people took it like he was saying ‘women shouldn’t work’ and ‘women should be at home in the kitchen cooking and having babies.’ He didn’t say that!” Indeed, the backlash to Butker’s comments was far more wide-ranging than many worse athlete quotes in recent years. item.title: No envy, no secrets: How Spain's Gipuzkoa became football coaching hotbed
item.description: Liverpool's Basque head coach Andoni Iraola will face former Antiguoko team-mates Xabi Alonso and then Mikel Arteta in quick succession (Paul Currie) Premier League heavyweights Liverpool, Arsenal and Chelsea clash this week with an unlikely thread linking them -- the men in charge all hail from the small Basque province of Gipuzkoa. Andoni Iraola's Liverpool host Xabi Alonso's Chelsea in the League Cup on Wednesday, and then Mikel Arteta's English champions Arsenal on Sunday 1 in the Premier League Unai Emery, a fourth Premier League coach from Gipuzkoa, takes Aston Villa to face giants Barcelona on November 3 in the Champions League. So how did Spain's smallest province, of just 1,980 square kilometres (765 square miles), with a population of around 730,000, produce 20 percent of the Premier League's coaches? A good starting point is one man, who mentored them all but, unlike Alonso or Arteta, is little known outside of the region -- 80-year-old Mikel Etxarri. "A wise man and a master of football, the teacher of teachers," Josu Zubia Ramos, the Gipuzkoa football federation's director of coaching, told AFP. Etxarri, whom the federation's coaching school is named after, has worked tirelessly for over half a century to spread his ideas. "We Basque coaches have been fortunate to have a very strong bond between us," Etxarri told AFP, days after he was honoured for his career at a friendly between Real Sociedad and Athletic Bilbao in October. "I think we've been lucky enough to live professional football without being professionals in that sense, without showing that passion for money, but rather a passion for knowledge." Once, when asked about why coaches from the region were so successful, Arteta highlighted the "passion" of his people and "the education we all got". An education which began as kids. Arteta, Iraola and Alonso all played in the same midfield aged eight -- for youth football club Antiguoko Kirol Elkartea, in San Sebastian. Their shirts hang in the club offices, with the coaches never forgetting their roots. Current Arsenal midfielder Martin Zubimendi is another Antiguoko graduate. - Overcoming limited resources - Historically, Real Sociedad and Athletic Bilbao have provided Basque football's core. Athletic, based in neighbouring Bizkaia, still operates its famous local player policy, while Real Sociedad abandoned its own restrictions on signing players from outside the region in 1989, but their academy remains an important source. The pathway from academy to first team seems clearer than at other clubs, with players focused on how to compete for their local team, and give back afterwards. Their fans expect success despite their limited resources compared to giants Real Madrid and Barcelona. Some of that gap is made up for in work rate and competitive spirit. item.title: Humble hero Kane the perfect heir to Matthews as Ballon d'Or comes 'home'
item.description: Humble hero Kane the perfect heir to Matthews as Ballon d'Or comes 'home' originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . PALLADIUM THEATRE, LONDON — Harry Kane felt like London was a good omen as the moment of truth arrived at the most closely contested Ballon d'Or in years. Kylian Mbappe can reasonably claim to be the most fearsome player on the planet right now, while there are surely none more lavishly gifted than Lamine Yamal. But no one was better, scored more relentlessly or realised their talents to a fuller extent than England's captain marvel in 2025/26. Mbappe and Lamine each have more Ballon d'Or runs in their futures. That's not to say Kane doesn't. Sure, he's 33, but he is playing the best football of his career in a Bayern Munich team that is better than any other he has spearheaded. He'll also, barring something completely unforeseen, be England's centre-forward at Euro 2028, where the great quest to bring football home will continue. "I think it's massive for England, for our country. Being here in London was as a good omen for me," Kane said after joining Stanley Matthews, Bobby Charlton, Kevin Keegan and Michael Owen as a Ballon d'Or winner from the home of football. "It's been too long. We've had so many great players, and those greats from when I was growing up couldn't get this award. "I'm extremely proud to put us back on the map. Playing for England is my biggest honour, the thing I love to do the most. Winning a major honour with England is the number one priority, that's for sure." MORE: Ballon d'Or 2026 ceremony from London as it happened The Ballon d'Or did not come home here – it is an eminently French concern – but it returned to its roots in a fashion. The ceremony took place in England to mark its 70th anniversary and commemorate the inaugural winner, the Stoke City and Blackpool great Matthews. 'The Wizard of Dribble' enjoyed a career of implausible longevity and was 41 when he lifted the prize that would become football's most coveted gong. A selfless, quiet man known for an obsessive dedication to honing his craft, Matthews was a footballer in whom Kane might see plenty of himself. The Baltimore Ravens could be getting their biggest offensive weapon back at just the right time, as head coach Jesse Minter expressed optimism Monday about quarterback Lamar Jackson potentially returning for Sunday's matchup against the Buffalo Bills . Jackson has missed Baltimore's last three games after suffering a high left ankle sprain against the Tennessee Titans on October 4. His absence has created significant challenges for a Ravens offense struggling to find consistency. Minter believes the two-time NFL MVP is making progress, although his availability remains uncertain. "I think he was able to get in a little bit of work obviously towards the end of last week," Minter told reporters Monday . "And so I think he'll be in a decent spot, but we'll know a lot more on Wednesday." Jackson appeared close to returning against the Cincinnati Bengals after participating in limited practices throughout the week. However, Baltimore ruled him out Saturday, leaving Tyler Huntley to make another start. The Ravens suffered a disappointing 35-13 defeat despite building a 13-0 halftime advantage. Huntley threw for a career-high 298 yards, but Baltimore's offense struggled to finish drives while Cincinnati dominated the second half. Without Jackson, the Ravens have averaged just 17.7 points per game over their last three contests. Despite those struggles, Minter refuses to use Jackson's absence as an excuse. "Lamar's 1 of 1, right? Two-time MVP, obviously a high-caliber player, but I just don't like the built-in excuse of why things are going a certain way," Minter said. Baltimore enters Sunday's matchup with a 4-3 record, sitting last in the AFC North. Jackson's potential return would provide a significant boost against a talented Buffalo team, particularly because his mobility creates problems for opposing defenses. However, Baltimore must ensure its franchise quarterback is completely healthy before putting him back on the field. With playoff positioning becoming increasingly important, the Ravens desperately need Jackson's leadership and explosive playmaking ability to reverse their recent struggles. Wednesday's practice could determine whether Baltimore gets its superstar back for this crucial matchup. Speaking to L’Equipe , Garcia said that Kane beat Mbappé to world football’s greatest individual prize by fewer than 41 points, which was the small gap that separated Vinicius Junior to Manchester City’s Rodri back in 2024. The Men’s Ballon d’Or is decided by 100 journalists – one from the top 100 nations in the FIFA rankings – who draw up their list of the ten best players from the past season.
